text: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do when they assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra, eager for battle?
Then Arjuna, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra drawn up for battle, spoke to Krishna as his chariot was placed between the two armies.
The Supreme Lord said: You speak of learned words but grieve for what is not worthy of grief. The wise lament neither for the living nor for the dead.
Just as the embodied soul continuously passes from childhood to youth to old age, similarly, at death, the soul passes into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
The soul is neither born nor does it die at any time. It is unborn, eternal, primeval, and is not slain when the body is slain.
As a person sheds worn-out garments and puts on new ones, so the soul sheds worn-out bodies and enters new ones.

You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself to be the cause of the results of your activities, nor be attached to inaction.
Be steadfast in yoga, O Arjuna. Perform your duty equipoised, abandoning all attachment to success or failure. Such equanimity is called yoga.
Endowed with wisdom, you shall free yourself from both good and evil results. Therefore, devote yourself to yoga, which is skill in action.
One who is not disturbed by the threefold miseries, who is not elated by happiness and free from attachment, fear, and anger — such a sage is called a muni.
While contemplating the objects of the senses, attachment develops. From attachment, desire arises. From desire, anger is born.
From anger comes delusion; from delusion, bewilderment of memory; from loss of memory, the destruction of intelligence; and from destruction of intelligence, one perishes.
Perform your prescribed duty, for action is superior to inaction. Without action, you cannot even maintain your body.
Therefore, without attachment, perform your duty, for by working without attachment one attains the Supreme.
Whatever a great person does, others follow. Whatever standards they set, the world follows.
The wise should not create confusion in the minds of the ignorant. Acting with devotion, they should set an example.
Whenever there is a decline in righteousness and a rise in unrighteousness, O Arjuna, I manifest Myself.
For the protection of the righteous and the destruction of the wicked, I appear millennium after millennium.
As all surrender unto Me, I reward them accordingly. Everyone follows My path in all respects, O son of Pritha.
Content with what comes without effort, free from duality, without envy, and equipoised in success and failure — such a person is never entangled.
One who performs actions without attachment, offering them to the Supreme, is untouched by sin — just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
The humble sage sees with equal vision a learned Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste.
Elevate yourself through your own mind, not degrade yourself. The mind is the friend of the self, and also its enemy.
For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. But for one who has failed to do so, the mind is the greatest enemy.
Let the yogi constantly concentrate the mind on the Self, remaining in seclusion, alone, with controlled mind and body, free from desires.
The Supreme Lord said: O mighty-armed Arjuna, it is true that the mind is restless and difficult to control, but through practice and detachment, it can be tamed.
Among thousands of persons, hardly one strives for perfection. Among those who strive, hardly one truly knows Me.
I am the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and passion. I am desire that is not contrary to righteousness, O lord of the Bharatas.
Therefore, remember Me at all times and fight. With mind and intellect fixed on Me, you will surely attain Me.
After attaining Me, the great souls never return to this temporary world of misery, for they have achieved the highest perfection.
This knowledge is the king of sciences, the most secret of all secrets. It is the purest knowledge, directly perceivable, righteous, and eternal.
To those who worship Me with undivided devotion, I provide what they lack and preserve what they have.
Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give — do it as an offering to Me.
One who knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the Supreme Lord of the universe is undeluded among mortals and liberated from all sins.
I am the source of all spiritual and material worlds. Everything emanates from Me. The wise remember this and worship Me with devotion.
The Supreme Lord said: I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds. I have come here to destroy all people. Even without you, all these warriors will cease to exist.
Fix your mind on Me alone and surrender your intellect to Me. Without doubt, you will dwell in Me alone.
One who is free from malice, friendly to all beings, without possessiveness, free from ego, and equipoised in pain and pleasure — such a devotee is dear to Me.
One who does not agitate the world and who is not agitated by the world, who is free from joy, anger, fear, and anxiety — such a person is dear to Me.
Humility, modesty, non-violence, patience, honesty, service to the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control — these are declared as knowledge.
Detachment from sense objects, absence of ego, perception of the pain of birth, death, old age, and disease — this is knowledge.
Among these, sattva is pure and illuminating. It binds the soul through attachment to happiness and knowledge.
Rajas is passionate, born of desire and attachment. It binds the soul through attachment to action and its fruits.
Tamas is born of ignorance and deludes all embodied beings. It binds through negligence, laziness, and sleep.
Free from pride and delusion, having conquered attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self with desires subdued — such persons attain that eternal state.
The eternal soul in the body is a fragment of My own being. It attracts the senses and the mind, which reside in nature.
The Supreme Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, perseverance in knowledge, charity, control of the senses, sacrifice, study of scripture, austerity, and honesty — these are divine qualities.
There are three gates to hell: lust, anger, and greed. Every intelligent person should abandon these, for they lead to the degradation of the soul.
Speech that is truthful, pleasant, beneficial, and not agitating to others is considered austerity of speech.
Charity given without expectation of return, at the right time and place, to a worthy person, is considered sattvic charity.
The Supreme Lord said: Renunciation of actions motivated by desire is called sannyasa, while abandoning the fruits of all actions is called tyaga.
For one who is not a renunciant, the threefold results of action — desirable, undesirable, and mixed — accrue after death. But for those who have renounced, there are no such results.
By worshiping the Lord, who is the source of all beings and who pervades all, one can achieve perfection through performing one's own work.
Abandon all varieties of religion and surrender unto Me alone. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.
Where there is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, and Arjuna, the supreme archer, there will certainly be prosperity, victory, glory, and righteousness.
